item.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and environmental drivers of older pedestrian traffic crashes in Hong Kong: a spatial machine learning approach
item.dc:title: Spatiotemporal dynamics and environmental drivers of older pedestrian traffic crashes in Hong Kong: a spatial machine learning approach
item.dc:creator: Jian Liu Ketong Shen Farasath Hasan Xintao Liu Department of Land Surveying and Geospatial Science, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong, ChinaJian Liu is a PhD candidate in the Department of Land Surveying and Geospatial Science, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. His research interest focuses on urban informatics, human mobility, and accessible & inclusive cities.Ketong Shen received his PhD degree from the Department of Land Surveying and Geospatial Science, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. His research interest focuses on urban informatics, human perceptions, and social inequality.Farasath Hasan is a PhD candidate in the Department of Land Surveying and Geospatial Science, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. His research interests are urban informatics, spatial analysis, and urban growth dynamics.Xintao Liu is an Associate Professor in the Department of Land Surveying and Geospatial Science, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. He obtained his PhD from the Royal Institute of Technology (KTH). His research focuses on GIScience, transportation geography, and complex networks, aiming to leverage state-of-the-art technologies to advance smart cities and improve urban life, and he is particularly interested in integrating machine learning into modeling human behavior and analyzing human-environment interaction in cyber and physical spaces. He currently holds various academic leadership positions, including Chair of the Commission on Geospatial Analysis and Modeling for the International Cartographic Association (ICA), and Secretary-General of the Hong Kong GIS Association.

item.title: From heterogeneous signals to consistent wind fields: a unified framework for sea surface wind speed retrieval with multi-GNSS reflections

item.dc:creator: Ziheng Wu Fei Guo Zhiyu Zhang Zheng Li Xiaohong Zhang a School of Geodesy and Geomatics, Wuhan University, Wuhan, Chinab School of Surveying and Mapping, Xi’an University of Science and Technology, Xi’an, Chinac Chinese Antarctic Center of Surveying and Mapping, Wuhan University, Wuhan, ChinaZiheng Wu is currently a Ph.D. candidate at Wuhan University. He received the M.Sc. degree from the School of Geodesy and Geomatics, Wuhan University, in 2024. His current research focuses on GNSS reflectometry.Fei Guo is currently a professor at the School of Geodesy and Geomatics, Wuhan University. He received his B.Sc. degree in Survey Engineering from Nanjing Forestry University in 2007. He obtained his M.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees with distinction in Geodesy from Wuhan University in 2009 and 2013. His current research mainly focuses on GNSS precise positioning and its application in geoscience.Zhiyu Zhang is currently a postdoctoral researcher at the School of Geodesy and Geomatics, Wuhan University. He received the M.Sc. and Ph.D. degrees from Wuhan University. His research interests include GNSS reflectometry, soil moisture retrieval, and machine-learning-based remote sensing methods.Zheng Li is currently a lecturer at Xi’an University of Science and Technology. He received his B.Sc. and M.Sc. degrees from Xi’an University of Science and Technology in 2018 and 2021, respectively. He received his Ph.D. degree from Wuhan University in 2025. His current research focuses on GNSS Reflectometry.Xiaohong Zhang is currently a professor at Wuhan University. He obtained his B.Sc., M.Sc., and Ph.D. degrees with distinction in Geodesy and Engineering Surveying from Wuhan University in 1997, 1999, and 2002. His main research interests include Precise Point Positioning (PPP), GNSS/INS navigation, and their applications in geoscience and engineering.
